title: Reorder Into Even Steps
statement:
You get an array arr. Return true if its values can be put in some order where every neighbour differs from the previous one by the same amount (an arithmetic sequence). The common difference may be 0 or negative.

Every element must be used exactly once.

examples.why: In the order 1, 4, 7 every step is +3.
Sorted it is 2, 4, 6, 9. The first steps are +2 but the last one is +3.
A repeated value forces a step of 0, but 5 needs a step of 2. Spreading min to max evenly would ask for steps of 1, and 4 is missing.

hints: If the values form such a sequence, where do the smallest and the largest value sit?
Sort the array. Then only one order is possible, so check that every neighbouring difference is the same.
Without sorting: the step must be (max − min) / (n − 1). Each value must sit on that grid, and no grid spot may be used twice.

explain.intuition:
An arithmetic sequence is either rising, falling or flat, so sorting it gives the rising version. That means you never have to search for an order: sort, and the sorted order is the only candidate. Then compare every gap with the first one.

You can also skip the sort. The step is fixed by the ends: d = (max − min) / (n − 1). If d is not a whole number, fail. If it is 0, every value must equal min. Otherwise each value must be min + j·d for some slot j, and the n values must fill n different slots. A set of seen slots checks that in O(n).
steps: For each i from 2, if arr[i] − arr[i − 1] !== d, return false.
pitfalls: Sorting with the default JavaScript sort(), which compares numbers as strings: [10, 9, 8] stays as is.
In the O(n) version, checking only that each value is on the grid. [1, 1, 5, 5] passes that test but uses slots twice.
Dividing by zero when every value is equal and d = 0.

complexity.time: O(n log n) with sorting, O(n) with the slot set
complexity.space: O(1) extra after sorting, O(n) for the set

solutions.title: Sort and compare gaps
solutions.idea: The only possible order is the sorted one. Check that every gap equals the first.

solutions.title: Grid slots without sorting
solutions.idea: The step is (max − min) / (n − 1). Every value must land on its own slot of that grid.
